i < size; ++i) {\n        const double ref = reference[i];\n        const double res = result[i];\n        if (std::abs(ref) < 1e-10) {\n            // For very small values, check absolute error\n            if (std::abs(res) > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e\\n\", i, ref, res);\n                return false;\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Check relative error\n            const double relError = std::abs((res - ref) / ref);\n            if (relError > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e (rel error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, ref, res, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of rows/columns in the matrix (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -s <num>     Sparsity: 1 out of N entries is non-zero (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of iterations (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -m <val>     Maximum value for matrix and vector elements (default: 1.0)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    index_t numRows = 1024;\n    index_t sparsity = 10;\n    index_t iterations = 10;\n    double maxVal = 1.0;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numRows = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-s\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            sparsity = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-m\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            maxVal = atof(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Calculate number of non-zero elements\n    const index_t nItems = (numRows * numRows) / sparsity;\n\n    printf(\"Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SpMV) Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %u x %u\\n\", numRows, numRows);\n    printf(\"Sparsity: 1 out of %u entries is non-zero\\n\", sparsity);\n    printf(\"Non-zero elements: %u (%.2f%% sparse)\\n\", \n           nItems, 100.0 * (1.0 - static_cast<double>(nItems) / (numRows * numRows)));\n    printf(\"Iterations: %u\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Max value: %.2f\\n\", maxVal);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Allocate and initialize data structures\n    std::vector<double> h_val(nItems);                  // Non-zero values\n    std::vector<index_t> h_cols(nItems);                // Column indices\n    std::vector<index_t> h_rowDelimiters(numRows + 1);  // Row delimiters\n    std::vector<double> h_vec(numRows);                 // Dense vector\n    std::vector<double> h_out(numRows);                 // Output vector\n\n    printf(\"Initializing data structures...\\n\");\n    fill(h_vec.data(), numRows, maxVal);\n    fill(h_val.data(), nItems, maxVal);\n    initRandomMatrix(h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(), nItems, numRows);\n\n    // For validation, compute reference solution\n    std::vector<double> h_reference;\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Computing reference solution...\\n\");\n        h_reference.resize(numRows);\n        spmvCpu(h_val.data(), h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(), \n                h_vec.data(), numRows, h_reference.data());\n    }\n\n    // Perform SpMV computation\n    printf(\"Computing SpMV...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    for (index_t iter = 0; iter < iterations; ++iter) {\n        spmvCpu(h_val.data(), h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(),\n                h_vec.data(), numRows, h_out.data());\n    }\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate performance metrics\n    const double gflops = (2.0 * nItems * iterations) / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    const double avgTime = duration.count() / static_cast<double>(iterations);\n    \n    printf(\"Average time per iteration: %.3f ms\\n\", avgTime);\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(h_out, \"OutputVector\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        const bool valid = verifyResults(h_reference.data(), h_out.data(), numRows);\n\n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n","numLines":262,"startLine":1,"totalLines":262}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01NA7oCo4LvdBQU6Er9Dp9aL","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4UWDAJ1c7dyoBtLxSd6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've parallelized `spmv/spmv.cpp` with MPI, and the results match the original sequential code exactly. I updated `CMakeLists.txt` to use `find_package(MPI REQUIRED)` and link `MPI::MPI_CXX`. The executable is still `spmv`, and no files were added.\n\n**Testing:** I compared the `-r` output block against a standalone copy of the original sequential algorithm, which I rebuilt in `/tmp` because I had overwritten the original source. Seven configurations (including edge cases like a fully dense matrix and a nearly empty one) gave identical results on 1, 3 and 8 ranks. Validation with `-v` passes. I did not measure scaling beyond one small run (n=4000, 4 ranks, 5.8 GFLOPS).\n\n**How it works:**\n- **Matrix generation:**\n  - The original draws one `rand()` value per matrix entry, in order, which is the real cost at scale.\n  - I reimplemented glibc's `rand()` with a jump-ahead, so each rank starts at its own position in the original stream and generates only its rows.\n  - The jump-ahead is exact only for glibc's `rand()`, which is what this machine uses.\n  - Generation is now O(n²/P) per rank.\n- **Nonzero counts across ranks:**\n  - The original's \"exactly n nonzeros\" rule carries a count from one row to the next.\n  - Each rank first counts its hits assuming that rule doesn't apply, then the counts are chained across ranks.\n  - Only a rank whose range could reach the cap or the fill-remaining tail regenerates its rows exactly, which is normally just the last rank.\n  - Each rank then draws its matrix values from the right place in the stream.\n- **SpMV iterations:** rows are split into blocks, and the dense vector is generated on every rank. The timed iterations therefore need no communication.\n- **Timing:** it is barrier-synchronized, and the reported time is the maximum across ranks.\n- **Output and validation:** only rank 0 prints. `-r` gathers the output vector to rank 0, and `-v` verifies each rank's slice and combines the results.\n\n**Differences from the original:**\n- The program now prints an extra `MPI ranks: N` line.\n- Positions in the random stream are 64-bit, so matrices with `n ≥ 65536` don't hit the original's 32-bit overflow.\n- Every rank holds the full dense vector, which costs O(n) memory per rank."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":546,"cache_read_input_tokens":32526,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":546},"output_tokens":734,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c300f258-c53c-47d3-b02d-6a857e3be2a1","uuid":"770eaa54-4d07-479c-9028-9e91ec898475","timestamp":"2026-10-15T18:12:27.073Z","request_id":"req_011Cg4UWCcZk81x3kbev3SKb"}

I did not measure scaling beyond one small run (n=4000, 4 ranks, 5.8 GFLOPS).\n\n**How it works:**\n- **Matrix generation:**\n  - The original draws one `rand()` value per matrix entry, in order, which is the real cost at scale.\n  - I reimplemented glibc's `rand()` with a jump-ahead, so each rank starts at its own position in the original stream and generates only its rows.\n  - The jump-ahead is exact only for glibc's `rand()`, which is what this machine uses.\n  - Generation is now O(n²/P) per rank.\n- **Nonzero counts across ranks:**\n  - The original's \"exactly n nonzeros\" rule carries a count from one row to the next.\n  - Each rank first counts its hits assuming that rule doesn't apply, then the counts are chained across ranks.\n  - Only a rank whose range could reach the cap or the fill-remaining tail regenerates its rows exactly, which is normally just the last rank.\n  - Each rank then draws its matrix values from the right place in the stream.\n- **SpMV iterations:** rows are split into blocks, and the dense vector is generated on every rank. The timed iterations therefore need no communication.\n- **Timing:** it is barrier-synchronized, and the reported time is the maximum across ranks.\n- **Output and validation:** only rank 0 prints. `-r` gathers the output vector to rank 0, and `-v` verifies each rank's slice and combines the results.\n\n**Differences from the original:**\n- The program now prints an extra `MPI ranks: N` line.\n- Positions in the random stream are 64-bit, so matrices with `n ≥ 65536` don't hit the original's 32-bit overflow.\n- Every rank holds the full dense vector, which costs O(n) memory per rank.","ttft_ms":2129,"type":"result","duration_ms":303280,"uuid":"3c1313b4-606a-4eb0-9232-7cb29a8f375f","ttft_stream_ms":1445,"time_to_request_ms":145,"first_content_frame_ms":1446,"queued_turn_count":0,"result_index":0}
